q: ____ theory explains how chemical reactions occur.
e: Collision theory explains how chemical reactions occur. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Collision theory is based on the kinetic molecular theory of ____.
e: Collision theory is based on the kinetic molecular theory of gases. Collision theory says particles must hit with the right orientation and enough energy or no reaction happens.

q: Reactant particles moving in random directions possess ____ energy.
e: Reactant particles moving in random directions possess kinetic energy. Kinetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Not all collisions between reactant particles result in the formation of reaction ____.
e: Not all collisions between reactant particles result in the formation of reaction products. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: For a reaction to occur, colliding particles must possess a certain minimum energy known as an ____ energy.
e: For a reaction to occur, colliding particles must possess a certain minimum energy known as an activation energy. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need to react.

q: During a collision, the spatial ____ of the reactant molecules is important to determine whether or not a reaction occurs.
e: During a collision, the spatial orientation of the reactant molecules is important to determine whether or not a reaction occurs. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: If the colliding particles have the incorrect orientation, they will ____ off each other.
e: If the colliding particles have the incorrect orientation, they will bounce off each other. Bounce is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The unsuccessful collisions with insufficient energy do not produce a ____.
e: The unsuccessful collisions with insufficient energy do not produce a reaction. Reaction is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: When the particles collide with the correct orientation, they must have enough energy for a successful collision (____ collision) to produce a reaction.
e: When the particles collide with the correct orientation, they must have enough energy for a successful collision (effective collision) to produce a reaction. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful collisions between reactant ____.
e: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful collisions between reactant particles. Particles is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the activated ____.
e: Reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the activated complex. Complex is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The activated complex is a temporary species formed by the reactant particles as a result of the collision before they form the ____.
e: The activated complex is a temporary species formed by the reactant particles as a result of the collision before they form the product. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: The more successful collisions there are, the more the activated complex leads to the rate of a reaction being ____.
e: The more successful collisions there are, the more the activated complex leads to the rate of a reaction being faster. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: In the molecular view of the matter, it is postulated that chemical reactions depend on the collisions between the reacting particles - atoms, molecules or ____.
e: In the molecular view of the matter, it is postulated that chemical reactions depend on the collisions between the reacting particles - atoms, molecules or ions. Ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Reacting particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) must collide in the correct orientation with sufficient energy to overcome the energy ____ to react.
e: Reacting particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) must collide in the correct orientation with sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier to react. Barrier is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the frequency of collision ____.
e: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the frequency of collision increases. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the proportion of particles with energy that is greater than the activation energy ____.
e: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the proportion of particles with energy that is greater than the activation energy increases. More successful collisions per second make the rate rise.

q: Collision theory can be used to explain the main factors such as concentration, temperature, pressure, and particle ____, affecting the rate of chemical reactions.
e: Collision theory can be used to explain the main factors such as concentration, temperature, pressure, and particle size, affecting the rate of chemical reactions. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The activation energy ($E_a$) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a successful collision to take place in a ____.
e: The activation energy (Ea) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a successful collision to take place in a reaction. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: During the progress of a reaction, an unstable intermediate which is known as an activated complex, having required minimum energy, is formed before producing a ____.
e: During the progress of a reaction, an unstable intermediate which is known as an activated complex, having required minimum energy, is formed before producing a product. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: In order to get the product, the reactants must pass through a short-lived, high-energy ____ state.
e: In order to get the product, the reactants must pass through a short-lived, high-energy transition state. Transition metals have a partly filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion.

q: The minimum energy that needs to be reached in this state is equal to the activation energy ($E_a$) for that ____.
e: The minimum energy that needs to be reached in this state is equal to the activation energy (Ea) for that reaction. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: Hence, the activation energy represents an energy ____ for the reaction, and it has a different value in different reactions.
e: Hence, the activation energy represents an energy barrier for the reaction, and it has a different value in different reactions. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: In an exothermic reaction, since the final product has ____ energy than that of the reactants, energy is released.
e: In an exothermic reaction, since the final product has less energy than that of the reactants, energy is released. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: Some energy is released when the activated complex leads to the formation of the ____.
e: Some energy is released when the activated complex leads to the formation of the products. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: When there is sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier, the formation of the product is ____.
e: When there is sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier, the formation of the product is favourable. Favourable is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If the energy is not enough, it cannot overcome the energy barrier and the decomposition of the product, that is, back to reactants will ____.
e: If the energy is not enough, it cannot overcome the energy barrier and the decomposition of the product, that is, back to reactants will occur. Occur is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A high $E_a$ means that relatively few collisions have the required energy to produce the activated complex, and hence, the reaction rate is ____.
e: A high Ea means that relatively few collisions have the required energy to produce the activated complex, and hence, the reaction rate is slow. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: With a low $E_a$, more collisions have sufficient energy to react, and the reaction rate is ____.
e: With a low Ea, more collisions have sufficient energy to react, and the reaction rate is fast. Fast is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an unstable intermediate $[H_2I_2]$ which exists for a short time and then breaks up to form two molecules of hydrogen ____.
e: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an unstable intermediate [H2I2] which exists for a short time and then breaks up to form two molecules of hydrogen iodide. Iodide is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.
